title: Add TP-group watchdog + automatic quarantine/recovery for stuck groups (metrics + alerts, mitigate false positives)
creator: Talia Benson
project: Multi-GPU (TP) stability fixes (Serving Runtime Performance: Kernel + Scheduling)
description:
Context
- We have recurring production hangs/timeouts where a tensor-parallel (TP) worker group stops making forward progress under sustained load (often streaming + mixed sequence lengths).
- Today, stuck TP groups can keep receiving work, amplifying 5xx/timeout rate and making mitigation harder (needs manual restarts/traffic shifts).

Goal
- Implement a per-TP-group forward-progress watchdog that detects “stuck” groups and automatically quarantines them (stop scheduling), then performs controlled recovery.
- Provide clear metrics/logs for oncall triage and alerting.
- Avoid excessive false positives (do not flap/quarantine healthy but slow groups).

Non-goals
- Not a full redesign of TP architecture or comm backend.
- Not replacing kernel/collective-level timeouts; this is a safety net + failure domain containment.

Proposed behavior (v1)
1) Forward progress model
- Each TP group exposes a monotonic progress signal updated on meaningful progress events (per-rank + group aggregate):
  - recommended: increment a group-level counter when a decode step completes OR when any rank reports a completed collective for the active microbatch.
  - watchdog reads (a) last_progress_timestamp and (b) last_progress_counter.
- Watchdog evaluation interval: 1s (configurable).

2) Stuck detection (mitigate false positives)
- Trigger only if ALL conditions are true:
  - No progress for >= WATCHDOG_STALL_SECONDS (default varies by deployment mode).
  - Group has in-flight work (not idle) AND has not been explicitly draining.
  - Stalled condition persists for N consecutive checks (e.g., 3) to smooth jitter.
- Additional “slow vs stuck” guardrails:
  - If the group is executing extremely long sequences, allow a higher threshold (use per-request expected step time bucket or p99 token latency multiplier).
  - If host is under global backpressure (scheduler queue high / GPU util saturated), do NOT suppress watchdog; but require the consecutive-check threshold.

3) Quarantine semantics
- Transition TP group state to QUARANTINED in scheduler (no new work scheduled).
- Fail/abort in-flight requests with a well-defined error code:
  - internal: TP_GROUP_QUARANTINED (mapped to 5xx for Hosted, surfaced with retryable signal)
  - include group_id, pool_id, model_id, reason in structured log.
- Maintain failure domain boundaries:
  - quarantine the TP group first; do NOT immediately restart the entire host unless repeated failures indicate host-level issue.

4) Recovery (controlled teardown + rejoin)
- For v1: controlled teardown of the TP group comm context and worker processes for that group (implementation-specific: restart worker subprocess OR re-init communicator and CUDA contexts if supported reliably).
- Cooldown after recovery: do not schedule onto the recovered group for COOLDOWN_SECONDS (default 30s) to avoid immediate re-trigger.
- Rate limiting:
  - Max resets per host per 10 minutes (configurable).
  - If exceeded, escalate to host-level cordon + page (prevents infinite loops).

5) Observability (required)
Metrics (names tentative; align with Observability Pack naming conventions):
- tp_group_watchdog_trigger_total{reason,model,pool,cluster,region}
- tp_group_quarantine_total{reason,...}
- tp_group_reset_total{reset_type,...}
- tp_group_time_since_progress_seconds{group_id,...} (gauge; consider sampling to avoid cardinality explosion)
- tp_group_inflight_requests{...}
- tp_group_quarantine_cooldown_active{...}
Structured logs/spans:
- "tp_watchdog_stall_detected" with fields: group_id, ranks, last_progress_age_s, inflight, active_collective, scheduler_state, model_id, request_ids_sampled (bounded), reason
- "tp_group_quarantined" + "tp_group_recovered" with timing

Alerts (SRE-owned, implemented via ENG-2408 but this ticket defines requirements)
- Page-worthy (Hosted pools):
  - watchdog triggers rate > X/min per pool AND correlated with timeout/5xx spike
  - resets-per-host > threshold (indicates flapping/host instability)
- Ticket-level:
  - any watchdog trigger in perf-canary nightly workflow

Acceptance criteria
- Functional:
  - When a TP group is artificially stalled (fault injection), the watchdog quarantines within threshold and stops new scheduling to that group.
  - Quarantine produces the required metrics + structured logs, and in-flight requests are failed quickly (bounded).
  - Recovery attempts occur and the group returns to service after cooldown.
- Safety/false positives:
  - Under heavy load but no actual stall (slow tokens), watchdog does not trigger above an acceptable rate (define target: < 1 false positive / 12h per 1k GPUs in perf runs).
  - Quarantine/reset rate limited; does not degrade fleet by repeated restarts.
- Operational:
  - Oncall can differentiate "comm stall" vs "kernel stall" vs "scheduler starvation" using the emitted reason + dashboard panels.

Implementation notes
- Integrates with scheduler TP-group state machine (ENG-2402): needs QUARANTINED state and a "do not assign" check on dispatch path.
- Requires instrumentation (ENG-2404): progress counter and timestamps must be available cheaply.
- Needs config knobs (PR-18473): WATCHDOG_STALL_SECONDS, WATCHDOG_CONSECUTIVE_CHECKS, RESET_RATE_LIMIT, COOLDOWN_SECONDS; defaults per Hosted vs Dedicated.

Links
- Confluence initiative: sources/confluence/eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/tp-group-watchdog-and-quarantine-initiative.json
- Design/root causes: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/tp-stability-hangs-root-causes-and-fix-plan.json
- Representative incident: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems/2025-02-13-tp-hang-us-east-sev1.json

Risk notes
- Watchdog false positives can be more damaging than the hang if it causes widespread quarantines. Must ship behind a feature flag with conservative defaults + canary gates.
- Cardinality: per-group metrics must be bounded; avoid group_id labels in high-volume production metrics (log group_id instead; aggregate metrics by pool/model/region).

rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (Hosted canary, flag ON for 1 pool):
- Enable watchdog for 1 high-load Hosted pool (us-east) with conservative thresholds.
- Monitor: watchdog_trigger_rate, quarantine_count, reset_count, timeout_rate, p95/p99 token latency.
- Rollback triggers: sustained false positive quarantines (trigger rate without timeouts), reset flapping (rate-limit hits), latency regression > agreed threshold.

Phase 2 (Hosted broader):
- Expand to additional regions/pools once 48h clean.

Phase 3 (Dedicated opt-in):
- Expose config flag in Dedicated runtime config; CS/Solutions can enable for impacted customers.

Phase 4 (Default-on decision):
- After SRE sign-off + perf-canary stable, evaluate default-on for Hosted; Dedicated remains opt-in until PM policy (PM-513).
open_questions: Should recovery be process restart (safer) vs communicator re-init (faster)? v1 preference: restart to avoid CUDA/NCCL weird states.
What is the right default WATCHDOG_STALL_SECONDS per model size + sequence length mix? Need data from tp-watchdog-thresholds experiments.
Do we want to fail in-flight requests immediately on quarantine or attempt a bounded retry/fallback to another group? (fallback policy likely separate workstream).
